summary: Livingston sits at the heart of California's Central Valley, and its economy orbits one unmistakable anchor: the massive Foster Farms poultry processing complex, one of the largest in the western United States, which makes this small city of roughly 14,500 an actual job center rather than a bedroom community — unusual for a town compressed into just 3.7 square miles. The landscape is dead-flat agricultural plain, with open-sky horizons in every direction and summer highs that regularly push past 100°F, though the 9.5 hours of daily sunshine and mild winters around 53°F lows keep the gray-sky blues away. A median home price near $340,000 against a $76,158 median household income yields a price-to-income ratio around 4.5 — meaningfully more accessible than coastal California, though the 15.8% poverty rate signals that affordability is relative and the local wage floor matters. The street grid is compact and connected rather than subdivided, but daily life is car-dependent, with Highway 99 threading just west of town serving as the corridor to Merced (20 minutes south) or Modesto (40 minutes north). Livingston is a working agricultural town that runs on poultry and row crops, not amenities — and that tradeoff is the entire calculation.
